title: Four-regime dichotomy classification
description: Classifies a settling (closure orbit) by its closure ordinal kappa into exactly one of four regimes: strict-finite (kappa < omega), scott-continuous (kappa = omega), transfinite-bounded (omega < kappa < omega_1), aperiodic (kappa >= omega_1). The dichotomy's equivalences are enforced by classifying-regime: base-finite <=> kappa-class = finite (strict regime); Scott-continuous closure <=> kappa-class in {finite, omega}; and H1 of the settling-associated sheaf vanishes <=> kappa-class in {finite, omega} (cohomology is concentrated in the transfinite and aperiodic regimes). For a finite base, kappa is a concrete finite count and the least fixed point is computed.

kappa.description: Concrete closure ordinal (finite case only): iterations to the least fixed point.

least-fixed-point.description: The settled value (finite case only): the Knaster-Tarski least fixed point.
